children: BofA Securities lowered its price target on FedEx Freight

, the newly independent freight transportation carrier, to $140 from $157 while keeping a Buy rating. It cited weaker shipment expectations and limited financial disclosure ahead of the company's first calendarized results in October. FedEx Freight shares were down 0.42% in premarket, and have fallen 17% since the company's spin-off in May.

BofA said the stock's underperformance against less-than-truckload peers mainly reflects the thin standalone disclosure and uncertainty after the company terminated Chief Commercial Officer Mike Lyons on September 2. The firm now expects shipments per day to fall 3.0% in the third quarter and 1.0% in the fourth, compared with earlier forecasts of 1.5% growth in both. CFO Marshall Witt said on a September 8 call that shipments fell by mid-single digits in the first half and that the company expects to exit 2026 flat to slightly positive.

BofA forecasts a third-quarter operating ratio of 86.3%, a 450-basis-point deterioration from the second quarter and worse than the company's typical seasonal decline of 310 basis points. It sees revenue per shipment excluding fuel up 2.5%, trailing a peer average of 3.7%.

title: FedEx Freight Stock Slips After BofA Cuts Target
